newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil supported by U.S. arb.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil supported by U.S. arb.

text.p: NWE fuel oil markets subsided very slightly with crude on Monday, but a U.S. arbitrage for Russian product lent some support to high sulphur cargoes, traders said.
High sulphur cracked barges were bid at $113 fob ARA, a dollar below Friday's level, and demand was slack.
At least 100,000 tonnes of Russian fuel oil had already been sold into U.S. destinations, for both bunkering and refining, and more was expected to be sold there this week.
This gave a floor for high sulphur cracked fuel, suffering from limited utility demand in northern Europe and Portugal.
Low sulphur cracked prices were steady around $129 fob NWE.
Traders reported steady buying interest in Italy. "There was a chance of sending material over to the U.S. last week, but that's no longer there.," one said.
Traders were split over the future direction of low sulphur prices.
